key_insight: The paper turns unambiguous pure-state discrimination into a smaller quantum-assisted SDP by using reciprocal states, reducing optimization to only N scalar variables while preserving a valid POVM under bounded Gram-matrix errors.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical NISQ-friendly route to quantum state discrimination with fewer variables and explicit robustness bounds, making measurement design more feasible on noisy hardware.
method: Represent the discrimination SDP in the span of chosen ansatz states using the NSS hybrid quantum-classical framework.
Choose the target states as the ansatz and use reciprocal-state representation to reduce the problem to N scalar optimization variables.
Derive error-aware rescaling and robustness bounds that guarantee a valid POVM from estimated overlaps.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the bounds with numerical simulations, study finite-shot scaling, and run IBM quantum hardware experiments to estimate pairwise overlaps and test the resulting POVMs.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate Gram-matrix estimation and the rescaling/robustness guarantees may still be conservative under hardware noise and finite-shot errors.
paper_title: Quantum-Assisted Unambiguous Discrimination of Pure States with Robustness Bounds
